To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a periarterial collagen collar placed around the carotid artery in the rabbit induces the appearance of the iNOS isoform of nitric oxide (NO) synthase in smooth muscle cells and that this NO production might contribute to the impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation of the carotid in this model.
iNOS expression is present in neointima of the rabbit model of atherosclerotic plaque formation and is not present before neointima is formed.
nitric oxide synthases isoforms II (iNOS) and III (eNOS) were detected in the neointimal cells of the rabbit aorta induced by a periarterial collar, but not isoform I (nNOS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
atherosclerosis and the role of nitric oxide.

the development of atherosclerotic lesions in a rabbit model, in which we have demonstrated the expression of inducible nitric oxide synthetase (NOS) in smooth muscle cells in the neointimal lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nitric oxide production by iNOS in smooth muscle cells is a component of the neointima that develops in the periarterial collar model of atherosclerotic plaque formation.
iNOS expression is not a cause of neointima formation but rather a consequence of neointima development.

nitric oxide synthases are expressed in the intimal smooth muscle cells of atherosclerotic plaques and may be responsible for the compromised endothelum-dependent relaxation observed both in this experimental model and in human coronary disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of iNOS in smooth muscle cells of neointima may play an important role in the development of atherosclerotic plaques and that the inhibition of iNOS may be an important target for the treatment of atherosclerosis.
the induction of iNOS is an early event in the development of a neointimal lesion and may contribute to the progression of this disease.
the inducible form of NOS is induced in smooth muscle cells in the neointimal lesions of the periarterial collar model of atherosclero-sis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inducible form of NOS, which is normally found only in macrophages and activated T lymphocytes, is also found in smooth muscle cells in the neointimal hyperplasia that occurs after a periarterial injury.
nitric oxide production by iNOS is induced in the neointimal smooth muscle cells of a rabbit model of atherosclerotic disease.
